docs: add EU Cyber Resilience Act stewardship guidance (#3526)

Human: @localden
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"localden"} -->
_Requested by **Den** · [project
thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Bzyr6VAkCeeUXG84MjhGvn?thread=cmsg_01Bzyr6VAkCeeUXG84MjhGvn5k6yDdsYhrcEf6CJAKPEuC)_

Add the Linux Foundation EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) stewardship
notice to the specification repository, which represents the project.

- `SECURITY.md` states that the project's software is ultimately
intended for commercial activities and adds the CRA stewardship
statement.
- GitHub Security Advisories are named as the emergency security
reporting mechanism. Reporters state at the start of the report that a
vulnerability is being actively exploited or that an incident is under
way.
- A new maintainer section says to notify a Core Maintainer or Lead
Maintainer immediately in `#security-disclosures` on learning of an
actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident, while fixing the
problem, never instead of fixing it. That Core Maintainer or Lead
Maintainer contacts the Linux Foundation CRA steward and works with the
steward, so the project speaks to the steward with one voice.
- `docs/community/policies.mdx` summarizes the above, and the
contributor ladder's escalation section points to it.

SDK and other repositories with their own `SECURITY.md` are not changed
here.

## Test plan

Prettier passes on the changed files. Not run locally: `npm run prep`
and `mint broken-links`.

docs: pull registry docs from v1.8.9 (#3480)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Den Delimarsky, David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1793430342149349)_

Squash-merge with this description as the commit message. The two
trailers on the last lines must stay in it, so that the next subtree
pull starts from this one.

**Before:** `docs/registry/` reflects the registry docs as of 2026-01-22
(registry commit 817e1216), plus six local edits made since. The FAQ
says servers cannot be deleted, the P-384 login command lacks the
`--algorithm` flag, the organization namespace rules are missing, and
the remote servers page says a remote URL can be used by only one server
name.

**After:** `docs/registry/` is byte-identical to
`docs/modelcontextprotocol-io` in modelcontextprotocol/registry at tag
`v1.8.9` (commit ba94f657). Seven pages change (+308/-25):
authentication, faq, github-actions, package-types, quickstart,
registry-aggregators and remote-servers.

## How

`scripts/pull-registry-docs.sh` was run against a clone of the registry,
first at `v1.8.7` and then at `v1.8.9`. The script splits
`docs/modelcontextprotocol-io` and squash-pulls the result into
`docs/registry/`. `npm run prep` passes, link check included.

The `v1.8.9` pull adds two upstream changes. Since `v1.8.8` several
server names can share one remote URL
(modelcontextprotocol/registry#1806), which replaces the sentence at
remote-servers.mdx L41. The aggregators page gains an "Efficient
synchronization" section (modelcontextprotocol/registry#1798).

A later run of the script was tested against a single squash commit that
carries these trailers. It merged cleanly and changed only
`docs/registry/`.

## Conflict resolutions

Three files conflicted in the `v1.8.7` pull. In each case upstream had
added content next to a line that a local commit had also touched, and
upstream already carried the local change, so upstream's side was taken.
The `v1.8.9` pull had no conflicts.

- `github-actions.mdx`: new troubleshooting row for the `"invalid
audience"` error.
- `package-types.mdx`: new paragraph on the `mcp-name:` token boundary,
placed before the Cargo section that both sides carry identically.
- `quickstart.mdx`: the npm account prerequisite reworded to apply to
package-based servers only.

## Local commits since January

All six are carried by upstream, so nothing needs to go upstream.

- 5abdf440 removed `.mdx` suffixes from internal links. Upstream did the
same in modelcontextprotocol/registry#1052, and no suffixed links remain
there.
- 31dae913 pointed the server.json schema link at
`draft/server.schema.json`. Upstream has it from
modelcontextprotocol/registry#884.
- 91dcd516 added the SSE deprecation note to remote-servers. It was
superseded locally by 85bbf0e2.
- 85bbf0e2 set the final SSE deprecation wording. Upstream has the
identical sentence from modelcontextprotocol/registry#1590.
- 0d17c43d changed `PyPi` to `PyPI` in the FAQ. Upstream has it at
faq.mdx L55.
- c0b35791 added the Cargo (Rust) package type section. Upstream has the
identical section from modelcontextprotocol/registry#1207 and
modelcontextprotocol/registry#1331.

## Upstream follow-ups for the registry repo (not fixed here)

1. `authentication.mdx` contradicts itself on stale DNS records. L81
says a stale TXT record left behind "will be tried first and cause
verification to fail". L404 says the registry tries all published keys
and a different key in another record does not take precedence. The code
agrees with L404: `VerifySignatureWithKeys` in
`internal/api/handlers/v0/auth/common.go` accepts the first matching key
and fails only when none match.
2. `quickstart.mdx` L130 and L134 install `mcp-publisher` from
`releases/latest`, while `github-actions.mdx` L14-17 tells readers not
to use that URL. The three workflow examples in `github-actions.mdx`
(L35, L115, L191) pin `MCP_PUBLISHER_VERSION: v1.8.1`, behind the
`v1.8.9` tag.
3. `registry-aggregators.mdx` L78 still says a `"deleted"` status
typically indicates a moderation takedown. Since publisher-managed
deletion (modelcontextprotocol/registry#893) publishers set that status
themselves. `moderation-policy.mdx` also needs attention. Neither
passage has changed upstream.

docs: working-group sponsored SEP process (#3529)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1794253161846999)_

**Before:** The contributing page told protocol-change proposers to
discuss the idea, build a prototype, and then find a sponsor. The SEP
guidelines defined a sponsor as an individual Core Maintainer,
Maintainer or WG Lead whom the author found by looking up
`MAINTAINERS.md`, tagging up to two Maintainers on the pull request, and
asking in `#general` after two weeks without a response. A SEP pull
request without a sponsor carried the `proposal` label, and the
`Sponsor` header held a GitHub handle.

**After:** The contributing docs follow the sponsorship rules of
[SEP-3398](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/3398), which the SEP
guidelines now cite in their introduction. A working group sponsors a
SEP, and that is the path the docs describe.

- Working group path: check whether the idea fits the current focus on
the [roadmap](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/development/roadmap),
bring it to the relevant working group, reach working group consensus
and draft a SEP the group wants to sponsor, then bring it to the Core
Maintainers for review.
- Core Maintainer sponsorship is noted in one place, the "Sponsors"
section of the SEP guidelines, as the exception: the Core Maintainers
agree to sponsor the SEP and designate a Core Maintainer to represent
them, and no separate working group approval is required. In general
Core Maintainers will not sponsor SEPs.
- The `Sponsor` header names the Maintainer or Core Maintainer who acts
on the sponsoring group's behalf, as in `Name (@handle), on behalf of
the Transports Working Group` or `Name (@handle), on behalf of the Core
Maintainers`. That person is responsible for the SEP's status and labels
and for tracking its implementation.
- When an idea falls in an interest group's area, the interest group can
start a working group for it through the [forming a
group](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/working-interest-groups#forming-a-group)
process, and that working group sponsors the SEP. When no working or
interest group covers the area, the author proposes a new working group
through the same process.
- A proposal developed in the open before it has a sponsor lives in a
draft pull request. It is not yet in the SEP process, has no SEP status,
and is marked by the `wg-support-needed` label. Once a working group
agrees to sponsor it, the pull request is marked ready for review and
the sponsor sets `draft`. The `proposal` label is no longer part of the
process.
- Authors who are not members of the `modelcontextprotocol` GitHub
organization ask the working group's leads or the sponsor to open the
pull request.

The "Before you write" paragraph that required a linked prior discussion
is removed. Workflow step 6 keeps its wording, so the sponsor still
confirms that the prior discussion is linked in the pull request
description.

How: `docs/community/contributing.mdx` replaces the "Discuss / Prototype
/ Find a sponsor / Write" steps with the four-step working group flow,
says that a SEP needs a working group or the Core Maintainers as
sponsor, and says in its last step that by then the author should be a
member of the working group with access to open pull requests on the
specification repository. `docs/community/sep-guidelines.mdx` cites
SEP-3398 in the introduction, lists the working group steps under
"Before you write" with the interest group and no-group cases, replaces
the awaiting-sponsor node in the workflow diagram with a draft pull
request stage, updates workflow steps 2, 4 and 5 and the `draft` row of
the status table, and rewrites "Sponsors" around working group
sponsorship and the named sponsor, with Core Maintainer sponsorship as
the exception. `docs/community/working-interest-groups.mdx` describes
the interest group to working group path. `CONTRIBUTING.md` says a SEP
pull request is marked ready for review once the working group has
agreed to sponsor it. `seps/TEMPLATE.md` gives the new form of the
`Sponsor` field. `plugins/mcp-spec/skills/draft-sep/SKILL.md` and
`plugins/mcp-spec/README.md` follow the same model: the `draft-sep`
skill sends authors to a working group, and without a sponsor it opens a
draft pull request for developing the idea in the open and says it is
not yet in the SEP process. `npm run prep` passes.

The `dormant` status, the 180-day rule, and queue scheduling and voting
are unchanged by this PR.

docs(community): list Core Primitives WG on working groups overview (#3544)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1793975038956449)_

Follow-up to #3513.

**Before:** The working groups overview lists 14 working groups and
omits Core Primitives. The roadmap names the group, and it has leads, a
repository and a weekly meeting.

**After:** The overview has a Core Primitives row with leads, Discord
channel and focus. The name links to the group's repository until the
charter in #3545 lands. The new row is wider than the old columns, so
the formatter realigns every row and the rest of the diff is whitespace.

## Sources

- **Leads:** the `core-primitives-wg-leads` team in Access ([roles.ts
L418-L428](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/access/blob/f89698a2e3206656d464c2ca203279cd1695ca4c/src/config/roles.ts#L418-L428))
has two members,
[kurtisvg](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/access/blob/f89698a2e3206656d464c2ca203279cd1695ca4c/src/config/users.ts#L582-L594)
and
[dsp-ant](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/access/blob/f89698a2e3206656d464c2ca203279cd1695ca4c/src/config/users.ts#L312-L335).
modelcontextprotocol/access#234 added the team.
- **Focus:** tool result shape, stability, and audience, the current
focus David gave in review on #3545. The Improved Primitives area comes
from the roadmap ([roadmap.mdx
L65-L77](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/ddbbf0f8ab3038a3406844e9ee063644eae57cc3/docs/development/roadmap.mdx#L65-L77)).
- **Discord:** the [calendar
events](https://meet.modelcontextprotocol.io/tag/core-primitives-wg)
link the
[channel](https://discord.com/channels/1358869848138059966/1540127738080534648).
The Discord API returns the name `core-primitives-wg` for that channel
id.
- **Repository:**
[modelcontextprotocol/core-primitives-wg](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/core-primitives-wg),
created through modelcontextprotocol/access#234.

## Questions for @kurtisvg and @dsp-ant

1. **Focus:** answered in review on #3545. The row now lists tool result
shape, stability, and audience.
2. The row links the repository for now. Once #3545 merges, the link
should move to the charter page. Should that be a follow-up PR, or
should this PR wait for the charter?

docs(seps): fix dead link targets in SEP documents (#3547)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1794253161846999)_

**Before:** The link scan over the rendered SEP pages reports 46 dead
links across six SEPs (SEP-2640, SEP-1865, SEP-1577, SEP-2133, SEP-2575
and SEP-3398). A reader who clicks one lands on a GitHub 404 page, or
nothing happens because the anchor does not exist on the page. Three
more links, in SEP-2133, SEP-3392 and SEP-3398, open the right page on
modelcontextprotocol.io and then fail to scroll to their section,
because the anchor in the URL no longer matches a heading.

**After:** 14 of these links resolve. In SEP-2640 the 8 links to the
`skills/list` and `skills/get` sections jump to those sections on the
docs site, and the SEP-3398 link to its Hard Freeze section does the
same. SEP-2575 links to the Transports WG decision document at its new
path. SEP-1577 links to `toolLoopSampling.ts` at the last commit that
contains the file. The working group decision-making links in SEP-3392
and SEP-3398 and the `_meta` link in SEP-2133 scroll to the intended
section. The scan now reports 35 dead links. They are listed below with
the reason each one is left alone.

**How:** Only link targets changed in `seps/*.md`. No link text, prose
or heading changed. Five of the six files are Final SEPs (SEP-3398 is
Accepted), and they were edited for links only with the maintainer's
go-ahead in the linked thread. The pages under `docs/seps/` were
regenerated with `npm run generate:seps`, and their diff contains the
same target changes and nothing else. `mint broken-links --check-anchors
--check-external --files "seps/**/*.mdx"`, run from `docs/`, went from
46 dead links to 35. That scan checks external URLs by status code only,
so the three anchors on modelcontextprotocol.io URLs were checked by
running the same anchor check on a scratch copy with those URLs
rewritten to site-relative paths. `npm run prep` exits 0 with no
warnings and leaves the tree clean. The environment the scan ran in
could reach github.com only, so 145 links to other hosts were not
checked in either run.

The docs site and GitHub build heading anchors differently when a
heading title contains `/` or a dash character, and one anchor cannot
work in both places. The 9 in-page anchors changed here follow the docs
site. They no longer scroll when the `.md` file is viewed on GitHub.

Dead links left as they are:

- SEP-2640: 30 in-page links to `#names`, `#frontmatter`, `#skill-uris`,
`#resources`, `#integrity-and-verification` and `#limits`. These are
level 5 headings. The docs site gives anchors to heading levels 1 to 4
only, so no target exists on the rendered page. The links work on
GitHub. A fix needs a change to the renderer or to the heading levels,
which is outside a links-only edit.
- SEP-1865: 4 author profile links (`liadyosef`, `olivierchafik`,
`jeromeswannack`, `antonpidkuiko`). The renderer builds these links from
the handles in the SEP header, so a fix means changing the handle text.
The matching accounts appear to be `liady`, `ochafik`, `jerome3o` and
`antonpk1`.
- SEP-2133: the link to `MAINTAINERS.md` in
`modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`. That repository has no such file on
`main` and its history shows none, so there is no successor to point to.
- SEP-2596: the link to
`/specification/draft/basic/transports#backwards-compatibility`, which
is outside the scan count. The draft transports page was split and the
HTTP+SSE guidance the SEP cites is no longer in the draft. The closest
match is the 2025-11-25 version of the page. Pointing there changes the
spec version the SEP cites, so it needs a maintainer decision.

commit.message:
fix(blog): keep code blocks dark in the light theme (#3542)

Code blocks on the blog are hard to read in the light theme: the syntax
colors are monokai's (made for a dark background), but the block is
drawn on light grey. Example:
https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/exploring-file-uploads-and-downloads-in-mcp/

## Cause

The inline code rule `.post-content code` sets `background:
var(--surface)`, and it also matches the `<code>` inside a `<pre>`. That
`<code>` is a block that fills the `<pre>`, so it covers the dark
`--code-paper` background set on `.highlight` and `pre`. In the dark
theme `--surface` is dark, so nothing looked wrong there.

## Fix

Set `background: var(--code-paper)` on `.post-content pre code`, so code
blocks are dark in both themes, as the comment on `--code-paper` already
says they should be.

## Testing

Not rendered locally (no Hugo on this machine). The change is one CSS
declaration; please check the preview in the light theme.

docs(community): state who can open pull requests and how to get there (#3534)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1794253161846999)_

**Before:** The docs gave three answers on who can open a pull request
in this repository. `docs/community/contributing.mdx` said "write
access", the contributor ladder said pull requests are "open to all",
and `CONTRIBUTING.md` said organization members while its step list said
to "request membership in the access repository", which records members
once the ladder's sponsorship requirements are met. The contributing
guide also pointed newcomers at the `good first issue` and `help wanted`
labels, which have no open issues in this repository.

**After:** One rule with one term. Only members of the
`modelcontextprotocol` GitHub organization can open pull requests on the
specification repository, and membership comes from being active on
issues or in working groups and interest groups. The contributing guide
states it, links the ladder's Member role for the requirements, and says
what a non-member does with a small fix: open a "Report a bug" issue or
raise it in the working group's channel, and a member or maintainer
picks it up.

**How:**

- `docs/community/contributing.mdx`: state the rule in "Change the
specification or docs", name the bug report form, say the first step is
enough for a typo, broken link or small specification bug, and name the
`draft` folders that fixes go in. The "Find your group" step now points
to open issues and the group's channel.
- `docs/community/contributor-ladder.mdx`: the Contributor row and
section no longer say pull requests are open to all, and the Member
privileges say plainly that Members can open pull requests on the
specification repository. No requirement or approval step changes.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: "Submitting Changes" says where membership comes
from, and step 2 links the Member role in place of the access
repository.

`docs/community/sep-guidelines.mdx` still says "collaborators" and the
SEP steps in `contributing.mdx` still say "write access". Both are left
to #3529, which edits those lines.

commit.message:
fix(sep-automation): drop the proposal state and sponsor-hunt comments (#3535)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1794253161846999)_

**Before:** The SEP lifecycle bot treated `proposal` as the first SEP
state. It moved a `proposal` SEP to `draft` as soon as one of its
assignees was a member of the `steering-committee` team tree. If a
`proposal` went quiet, the author got a reminder after 90 days that
asked "Do you need help finding a sponsor?", and after 180 days the bot
labelled the SEP `dormant` and closed it. A quiet `draft` got one of two
comments after 90 days: a "Sponsor Check-in" for the individual sponsor,
or "Core Maintainer Sponsor Needed" when no assignee was a core
maintainer.

**After:** The bot no longer has a `proposal` state. SEPs are only
accepted with a sponsoring working group, and people who want to develop
one in the open use a draft pull request. A quiet `draft` gets a single
"Draft Check-in" after 90 days. It is addressed to the author and the
current assignees, and it says that the sponsoring working group, its
leads and the author move the SEP forward. The bot no longer asks anyone
to find an individual sponsor.

## How

- `proposal` is removed from `SEPState`, the transition table, the state
label list, the staleness rules and the config, together with the
`proposal` to `draft` auto-transition. `PROPOSAL_PING_DAYS` and
`PROPOSAL_DORMANT_DAYS` are no longer read. Neither is set in any
workflow.
- `createAuthorPingComment`, `createSponsorPingComment` and
`createNeedsSponsorComment` are replaced by one
`createDraftPingComment`. The `sponsor` ping target, the `NeedsSponsor`
action and the "Needs Sponsor" section of the Discord summary go with
them.
- `sep-lifecycle.yml` no longer filters on the `proposal` label, and
`remove-labels-on-accept` in `slash-commands.yml` no longer lists it.
- New tests cover the recipients and wording of the draft check-in, and
that an item still carrying `proposal` gets no comment, no label change
and no close.

## Behaviour changes

1. **Items labelled `proposal`** (13 open today, none with a second
state label) have no SEP state for the bot and are left alone. The
90-day author reminder, the 180-day `dormant` label and close, and the
automatic move to `draft` on sponsor assignment all stop.
2. **Quiet `draft` SEPs** get the new "Draft Check-in" in place of
"Sponsor Check-in" or "Core Maintainer Sponsor Needed". The same SEPs
are pinged at the same times: 90 days without activity from the first
assignee (or the author when nobody is assigned), with the 14-day
cooldown. The comment now mentions the author and every assignee.
Before, it mentioned the sponsor only, or the assignees only.
3. **Accepting a SEP** no longer strips a leftover `proposal` label. The
bot ignores that label, so it has no further effect.
4. **Discord weekly summary** loses the "Needs Sponsor" section and
lists draft check-ins as author pings.

Unchanged: the 30-day reference implementation reminder on `accepted`
SEPs, the 14-day activity check for core maintainers assigned to `draft`
and `in-review` SEPs, and the bot's silence on `in-review`, `final`,
`dormant` and unlabelled items otherwise. The bot does not comment on,
relabel or close anything it left alone before.

## Left for the follow-up

Nothing schedules the mark-dormant action after this change, because
`proposal` was the only state with a dormant timer. The transition
handler is likewise no longer called by the processor. Both executors,
their comment templates and their Discord sections are left in place
here to keep this diff reviewable. The follow-up PR that introduces the
single inactivity close will reuse or remove them.

## Testing

`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass in
`tools/sep-automation` (7 files, 41 tests). `npm run prep` passes at the
repo root. It does not cover this package.

Pairs with #3529, which updates the SEP docs. The inactivity rule
follows in a separate PR.
